blocks.s: The first is purification from sins. The second is the studious anxiety and diligent labor of the mind to obtain the divine unction and grace, without which the mind is arid, as grass without dew and rain. The third is devout compunction of heart, in which love reigns and from which devotion is generated, and sorrow, which is the origin of confession. The fourth is compassion with one's neighbors in their adversities and rejoicing with them in their prosperities. The fifth is compassion of soul in the Passion, affliction, and persecution of Christ. The sixth is the small fire of burning desire, which is strong prayer before God. The seventh is the visitation of the Spouse, or the inflowing of the Word of God, which graciously descends into the thirsting soul like a river of peace, through the infusion of hidden consolation. The eighth is the contemplation of the mind aspiring upward, which faithfully contemplates the citizens of the homeland and the King of glory presiding over them. The ninth is the continual meditation on divine things, as it is written: "On his law he shall meditate day and night" (Ps. 1:2). The tenth is the overshadowing of the divine darkness in the chamber of the heart, when the mind has entered the darkness of incomprehensible light, with the eyes of the soul fixed on the infinite light, possessing God dwelling with her, resting under the shadow of the desired one (cf. Cant. 2:3). This pertains to mystical theology, and is the contemplation of God by negation or denial. The eleventh is mental excess or ecstasy, by which vehicle the devout mind, transported, is frequently joined through ecstatic contemplation to the company of the celestial citizens, and contemplates the face of God as closely and sincerely as can be done. The twelfth is the blessed death and entry into the homeland.
